answer: Could be: Slow-burst admission gate makes every new identity wait through a fixed quiet period, then send a shaped low-rate burst; tightly clustered arrivals are delayed as a group. Each identity pays forty-eight hours of continuous heartbeat traffic plus a distinct packet-timing profile, so an attacker repeats that time and bandwidth cost for every fake agent. A pearl of real traffic can pass the canyon, while karst-like timing gaps expose bursts that are too uniform. This has all three.
